rows.reason: Brave glossed as bold and unafraid; fearless matches; cowardly opposite and soldier/battle as fighting words are both true.
False claim: "cheetah and race come from racing". A cheetah is an animal, not something that comes from racing.
False claim: "towel and puddle are simply wet things". A towel is a thing for drying, not a wet thing; "simply" is also the banned word's family.
Chilly glossed as rather cool; cold is the only option in that sense; hot opposite, winter/frost cold-weather words. All true.
Shiny glossed as a bright glow; bright matches; dull opposite and mirror/gold as shiny objects are true.

Fault in the question as well as the script: FAIR is a three-sense headword the vr04 machinery retires from bare cards (register R1045/R1047 hold: which sense does the card carry?), and the key "just" is itself read by a child as "only". The gloss "even, square and right" also leans on the idiom "fair and square" a 9-11-year-old may not know.
Untrue claims: "It means bare and quite unfilled" (hollow does not mean bare) and "log and drum are hollow things" (a log is normally solid).
Huge glossed as very big; enormous matches; small at the far end, elephant and mountain big things. All true.

Wrong strength: "This word means fairly uncommon." Rare means not found often, not fairly uncommon; in a family whose distractors test strength, the gloss teaches the wrong one.
